messages:
sam: morning team, quick thread: we need a concrete playbook for producing "trace_export_token" for public telemetry sinks. privacy + compliance want no raw ids; analytics + billing need stable grouping.

jess: security constraints: irreversible by default, attorney wants no reversible mapping in exported buckets unless under strict legal process. any reversible cache must be audited + gated.

omar: infra constraints: we can either (A) HMAC-salt per-tenant and store 16B token, or (B) keep a reversible lookup backed by an encrypted KV. (B) is heavier: more writes, extra secrets surface, more ACLs.

tara: product: enterprise customers will ask for on-demand trace lookups tied to support tickets. timeline sensitive. we should design an opt-in enterprise flow.

sam: proposal outline: default = 128-bit keyed HMAC (tenant-salt) -> hex encoded 32-char token stored as `trace_export_token`. No raw trace id leaves stack. Enterprise customers can enable a short-lived encrypted audit-cache (opt-in) that maps token->raw for debug.

jess: +1 on default. audit-cache needs: KMS envelope encryption per-region, role-based retrieval, full access logs, and a manual support checklist before any lookup.

omar: numbers to consider: index width and storage. storing a 16B binary token is cheaper than a 32-char string in Postgres. Suggest `bytea(16)` or `varbinary(16)` depending on store. Also put a compact btree index on it.

sam: collision check: rough math for 10B total traces/year. For 128-bit space collision probability ~= n^2/(2*m) where m=2^128. Plugging numbers -> ~1e20/(2*3.4e38) ~ 1e-19 -> effectively zero. 64-bit would be too risky.

tara: can we support common customer queries? they do `trace_id:^abc` style prefix searches and they will break. needs doc & migration notes.

omar: we should avoid prefix-preserving tokens. If customers need prefix habits (rare), we provide a tenant-visible `trace_bucket` integer (e.g., trace_hash % 1024) for coarse routing, not the raw prefix. That preserves privacy while enabling group-by.

jess: note: `trace_bucket` leaks low-entropy info (collisions expected) but acceptable if documented and consented. include privacy review sign-off.

sam: ingest pipeline sketch:
```
# headers from services
X-RW-Trace: <raw-hex>
X-RW-Tenant: <tenant-id>

# pipeline
token = HMAC_SHA256(tenant_salt, raw)  # store as 16 bytes (first 128 bits)
emit trace_export_token = token
# drop raw before handing to public sinks unless tenant has audit-cache enabled
```

omar: storage impact estimate: at 30M traces/day, storing 16B token + base columns ~ adds 480MB/day raw token volume (pre-index). Indexes add ~20-30% overhead. Audit-cache for opt-ins is heavier: storing raw->token mapping ~ raw id (16B) + token (16B) + metadata -> ~1KB per entry after envelope, so 30 days for 10 pilot orgs ~ tens of GBs.

tara: rollout plan (phased):
- phase 0: dev-only PoC that emits both `trace_export_token` and raw to staging.
- phase 1: default-on HMAC export to non-sensitive sinks (metrics, prometheus exports). docs updated.
- phase 2: pilot audit-cache for 5 enterprise tenants behind FF + legal checklist.
- phase 3: console opt-in + retention slider + audit-log UI.

sam: migration details: dual-write `trace_export_token` alongside existing `trace_id` for 30d to let dashboards/saved queries move. backfill historical traces for last 90d for big customers (async job).

jess: access control: retrieval of raw from audit-cache requires 2-person approval for first lookup, and salted HMAC keys stored in KMS with restricted IAM. Log every retrieval with tenant id + ticket id.

omar: query compatibility: any place that used `LIKE 'abc%'` or prefix scans will break. Recommend running a compatibility scan across saved queries and dashboards: auto-flag obvious cases.

tara: product copy tweak: in console show: "Trace IDs obfuscated by default. Enterprise option: reversible debug retention (requires opt-in and audit)." Link to SLA/cost page that quantifies storage charge for audit-cache.

sam: open implementation choices:
- token length: 128 bits (recommended) vs 256 bits (stronger but larger index)
- encoding: store binary 16B vs hex 32-char -> binary is smaller in DB and index.
- audit-cache retention defaults: 7d vs 30d -> default 7d to reduce surface, allow per-org up to 90d.

jess: security: default 7d seems reasonable. legal may request longer; handle via contract additive.

omar: infra ops notes: if audit-cache enabled, ensure admission control on ingest to avoid extra 99th p99 CPU; use a write-ahead buffer + async persist to reduce tail latency.

sam: action items:
- omar: bench index size and write QPS for binary-16 vs hex-32 across our busiest DB cluster. due EOW.
- jess: draft audit-cache retrieval policy + minimal legal wording. due Tue.
- tara: draft console copy and pricing delta for audit-cache. due Wed.
- sam: write full RFC with migration playbook + backfill plan. will post here when ready.

ingest-bot: commit queued: feature/trace-export-token -> staging (poC) :package: 

tara: thanks all, please add any edge cases here. I'll run a customer impact pass tomorrow.

sam: thanks; cc'ing security & legal on RFC when posted.
